title: Going below zero
objectives: Place negative numbers on a number line and compare them
Add and subtract signed numbers as moves along the line
Explain why subtracting a negative moves you right

screens.title: Going below zero
screens.prose: Temperatures fall below zero, and bank accounts go into debt. We will give those amounts a place on the number line.
At 6 pm it is 3 °C. By midnight the temperature has fallen by 5 degrees.
screens.question: Drag the blue point to the temperature at midnight.

hints.text: A fall in temperature is a move to the left.
Count 5 steps left, starting from 3.
3 steps left reach 0. The last 2 steps go past zero.

feedback.correct: Five steps left from 3 ends two steps below zero.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count 5 steps left from 3.

byKey.lost-sign: You worked out 5 − 3 = 2 and stayed above zero. Count 5 steps left from 3: you pass 0.
byKey.stopped-at-zero: The fall does not stop at 0. Two more degrees take it below zero.

explain.text: From 3, five steps left pass 0 and stop two steps below it. We write that temperature as $-2$, read negative two. Numbers left of zero are **negative**.

screens.prose: A bank balance can go below zero: that means you owe money. Slide the balance left and right, past zero.
screens.question: Which balance is lower: −£7 or −£2?

options.why: You compared 7 with 2 and called −2 the lower one. A debt of £7 leaves you worse off: −7 is further left.

hints.text: Slide the balance to −7, then to −2. Which one is further left?

feedback.correct: −7 is further left, so it is lower.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Further left on the line means lower.

explain.text: On the line, $-7$ sits 5 steps left of $-2$. Further left is always lower, so $-7 < -2$. A bigger debt is a lower balance.

screens.prose: Numbers above zero are **positive** and numbers below zero are **negative**. You owe £4, so your balance is $-4$ pounds. Then you pay in £7.
screens.question: What is your balance now, in pounds?

hints.text: Paying in moves your balance to the right.
Start at −4 and count 7 steps right.
4 steps take you to 0. The other 3 take you to 3.

feedback.correct: $-4 + 7 = 3$: the debt is cleared with £3 over.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start at −4 and move 7 steps right.

byKey.wrong-way: You moved left, as if you had spent £7. Paying in moves right.
byKey.kept-sign: You found the 3 but kept the minus from the debt. The £7 cleared the debt and left £3 over.
byKey.sizes: You added 4 and 7. The debt uses up part of the £7, so take 4 from it instead.

explain.text: From $-4$, seven steps right pass 0 and land on 3. So $-4 + 7 = 3$. Adding a positive number is a move to the right.

screens.prose: A first trade makes £6. The second trade makes $-9$ pounds, a loss of £9. Your running total is $6 + (-9)$.
screens.question: Drag the total to where it stands after both trades.

hints.text: Adding a loss moves you left.
Start at 6 and count 9 steps left.
6 steps take you to 0. The other 3 take you below it.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start at 6 and move 9 steps left.

byKey.lost-sign: You found 9 − 6 = 3 but gave it a plus sign. The loss is bigger than the gain, so the total is below zero.

explain.text: Adding $-9$ moved you 9 steps left, the same move as taking away 9. So $6 + (-9) = 6 - 9 = -3$. Adding a negative number moves you left.

screens.prose: You start the week $-2$ pounds down. Two more losses follow: $-5$ pounds, then $-4$ pounds.
screens.question: Where does your running total end, in pounds?

hints.text: Each loss moves you further left.
Start at −2. Move 5 left, then 4 more.
−2 and 5 more to the left is −7. Then 4 more is −11.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Move left once for each loss.

byKey.two-negatives: You turned the losses into a gain. Adding losses only ever moves you left, so the total is below −2.
byKey.missed-one: You stopped after the £5 loss. The £4 loss moves you 4 more steps left.
byKey.cancelled: You let one loss cancel another. Every loss moves left; none moves right.

explain.text: Each loss moved you further left: $-2$, then $-7$, then $-11$. Losses pile up, so the total is $-11$, never positive. Adding two negatives makes a bigger negative.

screens.prose: Your balance is $-3$ pounds. The bank finds an error and removes a charge of £8. Removing that charge takes away $-8$: $$-3 - (-8)$$
screens.question: What is your balance now, in pounds?

options.why: You treated removing the charge as a new charge. Taking a charge away leaves you better off, so move right.
You found the gap between 3 and 8, then kept a minus. Removing the £8 charge lifts you past zero.
You added the sizes 3 and 8. The £3 debt came from that charge, so only £5 is left over.

hints.text: Does the bank's correction make you richer or poorer?
Without the £8 charge, your balance is £8 higher.
Move 8 steps right from −3.

feedback.correct: Removing the charge lifts you 8 steps, from −3 to 5.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Removing a charge raises your balance.

byKey.further-down: You treated removing the charge as a new charge. Taking away a debt moves you right, not left.

explain.text: Taking away a charge of £8 raises your balance by £8. So $-3 - (-8) = -3 + 8 = 5$. Subtracting a negative is a move to the right.

screens.prose: Adding a positive moves right. Adding a negative moves left. Subtracting undoes adding, so each move flips: $$a - b = a + (-b), \qquad a - (-b) = a + b$$
screens.question: Which is the same as $4 - (-6)$?

options.why: You dropped the second minus sign. Taking away −6 is not the same as taking away 6.
You moved the minus onto the 4. The 4 is untouched; only the −6 flips.

hints.text: Taking away −6 undoes a move of 6 to the left.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtracting a negative flips it into adding.

explain.text: Taking away $-6$ undoes a move of 6 to the left, so it moves 6 right. So $4 - (-6) = 4 + 6 = 10$.

screens.prose: Why does subtracting $-8$ add 8? Start from a line we can check on the number line: $$5 + (-8) = -3$$ Subtraction undoes addition, so taking the $-8$ back off must undo that move.
screens.question: Which line follows?

options.text: $-3 - (-8) = 5$, taking the $-8$ away returns us to 5
$-3 - (-8) = -11$, two minus signs push further down
options.why: You treated the two minus signs as another loss. Undoing a move of 8 left must move 8 right.
Adding $-8$ again moves 8 more steps left, to $-11$. Undoing needs the opposite move.

hints.text: Adding −8 took you from 5 to −3. What takes you back?
To undo adding a number, take it away. So $-3 - (-8)$ must land back on 5.

feedback.correct: Taking away what you added gets you back to where you started.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Undo the move from 5 to −3.

byKey.further: You treated the two minus signs as another loss. Undoing a move of 8 left must move 8 right.

explain.text: Adding $-8$ took 5 down to $-3$, so taking $-8$ away brings $-3$ back up to 5. And $-3 + 8 = 5$ as well. So $-3 - (-8) = -3 + 8$: subtracting a negative is adding.

screens.prose: A trader's running P&L, short for profit and loss, climbs to £120 on day 1. It then sinks to −£210 on day 3. The fall from a peak to the low after it is the **drawdown**.
screens.question: By how many pounds did the P&L fall from the peak to the low?

widget.label: Size of the fall in pounds

hints.text: The fall is the peak minus the low.
The peak is +120 and the low is −210.

feedback.correct: £120 down to zero, then £210 more below it.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the peak minus the low.

byKey.no-sign: You worked out 210 − 120 and ignored the sign of the low. The P&L fell 120 to reach zero, then 210 more.
byKey.negative: You have the right size. A drawdown is quoted as the size of the fall, so give 330.
byKey.neg-ninety: You took 210 from 120 without the minus sign on the 210. The low is −210, so you subtract a negative.

explain.text: Peak minus low is $120 - (-210) = 120 + 210 = 330$. The P&L fell £120 to reach zero and £210 more below it. Subtracting a negative low adds its size.

ideas: Negative numbers sit left of zero. Further left is lower: $-7 < -2$.
Adding a positive moves right, and adding a negative moves left.
Subtracting undoes adding, so subtracting a negative moves right: $a - (-b) = a + b$.

formula.name: Subtracting a negative
formula.note: Removing a debt of $b$ leaves you $b$ better off.

summary.trap: Removing a charge is not another charge: $-3 - (-8) = 5$, not $-11$.

options.why: You picked the smallest number after the minus sign. −3 is close to zero, so it is the mildest of the negatives.
Zero is not the lowest. Every negative temperature is below it.
You picked the second coldest. You picked the second coldest. −15 is 3 degrees lower than −12.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The coldest is the one furthest left on the line.

explain.text: On a number line $-15$ sits furthest left, then $-12$, $-3$ and 0. Furthest left is lowest, so $-15$ °C is coldest.

quiz.prose: Work it out as moves along the number line.
quiz.question: What is $-7 + 10$?

feedback.correct: Ten steps right from −7 lands on 3.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start at −7 and move 10 right.

byKey.wrong-way: You moved left. Adding 10 moves right.
byKey.kept-sign: You found the 3 but kept the minus. Ten steps right from −7 passes zero.
byKey.sizes: You added 7 and 10. The −7 uses up 7 of the 10 steps.

explain.text: From $-7$, seven steps right reach 0 and three more reach 3. So $-7 + 10 = 3$.

quiz.prose: It is −5 °C at night and 4 °C at noon.
quiz.question: How many degrees warmer is noon than the night?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find noon minus night, or count the steps between them.

byKey.sizes-minus: You took 4 from 5. The night is below zero, so count 5 up to zero and 4 more.
byKey.negative: You have the size right. Noon is warmer, so the rise is positive.
byKey.minus-one: You added −5 and 4. The rise is noon minus night: $4 - (-5)$.

explain.text: The rise is noon minus night: $4 - (-5) = 4 + 5 = 9$. On the line, 5 steps take $-5$ up to 0 and 4 more reach 4.

quiz.prose: A strategy's running P&L is −£150. The next day it loses another £75.
quiz.question: What is the running P&L now, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. A further loss moves the P&L further left.

byKey.as-gain: You moved right, as if the loss were a gain. A loss moves the P&L down.
byKey.sign: You added the sizes but dropped the minus. Both amounts are losses, so the total is a loss.

explain.text: Adding a loss of 75 moves 75 further left: $-150 + (-75) = -225$. The P&L is now £225 below zero.

quiz.prose: A debt of £4.25 is recorded, then removed again in full.
quiz.question: What is $-4.25 - (-4.25)$?

feedback.correct: Removing the debt brings you back to zero.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Taking away a number undoes adding it.

byKey.doubled: You added the debt twice. Subtracting −4.25 removes it.
byKey.sizes: You turned it into 4.25 + 4.25. Start from −4.25, then add 4.25.

explain.text: $-4.25 - (-4.25) = -4.25 + 4.25 = 0$. Any number minus itself is 0, negatives included.
